macos.fallback: installed_apps.list_inventory owns the pkgutil receipt roster (ecosystem macos_pkgutil)

windows.fallback: machine context only: per-user MSI products are never listed; measured as SYSTEM and as an admin user, non-elevated unmeasured

caveats: **Windows `list` and `product_codes` have no typed permission-denied path.** A failed `MsiEnumProductsA` loop looks identical to a genuinely empty product table — both fall through to the "no packages" sentinel row; only `list_inventory` reports an enumeration failure (a `constrained` status). All three actions now run inside one `try/catch`, so an exception yields a `constrained` status row and rc 1 instead of crossing the plugin ABI; their successful output is unchanged.

**macOS never reports a partial or empty list as complete, and `list` caps at 500 receipts.** A killed, timed-out, truncated, or nonzero-exit pkgutil run — checked across the whole walk, including every per-receipt `--pkg-info` call — emits a single `error|msi_packages: acquisition degraded (...)` row and rc=1 instead. Do not reintroduce a per-row emit-as-you-go loop; rows are buffered and committed only after the health verdict is known, because `write_output` cannot retract an already-appended row. A receipt DB with more entries than `kMaxPackages` gets an honest `msi|__truncated__|<total_seen>|-|-` sentinel row rather than a silently incomplete list.

**Linux is unimplemented, not merely leg-unsupported, and Windows `install_location` is usually empty.** `list` and `product_codes` unconditionally return `error|platform not supported` and rc=1 on Linux; no mechanism was bound (`list_inventory` answers `status|list_inventory|unsupported|linux:no_msi` with rc 0). On Windows only 4 of the 137 packages in the earlier `list` capture carried a real path (NordVPN network TAP, NordVPN network TUN, PlayStation Accessories, CMake): MSI's `InstallLocation` property is frequently left unset by the installer, so a `-` there reflects the source data, not a plugin gap.

**`list_inventory` drops nameless products and overlaps `installed_apps`.** It reads `InstalledProductName`, `VersionString` and `Publisher`, which Windows Installer defines only for installed products; a product that is advertised (assigned) but not installed is enumerated but reads as `inv|{code}|||`, and the collector drops an empty-name row (the API contract, not a probe: no advertised product was available to measure). The same product also normally appears as an `app`/`windows` row from `installed_apps`' registry walk, so a host carries two rows per MSI product; per-user products are never listed by `list_inventory`.

**A `list_inventory` enumeration error skips the whole installed-software cycle.** If `MsiEnumProductsExW` returns anything other than success or `ERROR_NO_MORE_ITEMS` (for example `1610`, a corrupt Windows Installer registration), the action is `constrained` and the daily sync skips that cycle for every source, `installed_apps` rows included, with skip reason `msi_packages.list_inventory:windows:msi_enum:<code>`. Nothing is deleted, but `last_seen` stops advancing and the skip repeats every cycle until the host's registration is repaired; the walk stops at the first error because the API allows no skip-the-bad-index-and-continue path.

definitions.description: Enumerates installed software packages: on Windows, Windows Installer (MSI) products via the MsiEnumProducts API, returning each package's product code GUID, display name, version string, and install location; on macOS, `pkgutil` package receipts, returning each package's reverse-domain identifier, a derived display name, version string, and install location. Useful for software inventory, patch compliance, and license auditing.

Lists the Windows Installer products installed for the whole machine (MsiEnumProductsExW in the machine install context, with MsiGetProductInfoExW for the name, version and publisher), in the form the daily installed-software inventory collects them. Per-user MSI products are never listed by this action. A property that cannot be read is an empty field, never a placeholder, and a product whose name cannot be read (for example one that is advertised but not installed) is listed with an empty name and is not collected by the inventory. Exactly one status row leads the result; zero products is a status row and nothing else. If the enumeration does not complete, the status row is `constrained` with a `windows:msi_enum:<code>` token and the products read so far follow it. macOS reports `unsupported` (installed_apps owns the pkgutil receipt roster) and Linux reports `unsupported` (no Windows Installer).
definitions.display_name: List Machine MSI Products For Inventory

definitions.description: Returns a compact list of installed package identifiers with their associated product names: MSI product code GUIDs on Windows, reverse-domain pkgutil package identifiers on macOS. This is a lightweight alternative to the full list when only product identification is needed, such as for uninstall targeting or compliance matching.

description: Enumerates installed packages and product codes (Windows MSI / macOS pkgutil)
how_it_works:
`list` enumerates installed packages and reports name, version, and install location per package. On Windows it walks `MsiEnumProductsA` and pulls `InstalledProductName`/`VersionString`/`InstallLocation` per product code via `MsiGetProductInfoA`. On macOS it runs `pkgutil --pkgs` to get the receipt ID list, then issues one `pkgutil --pkg-info <id>` call per receipt (bounded at 500 receipts) and derives a display name from the identifier's last dot-segment, since a receipt carries no separate name field. `product_codes` is the lighter sibling: it returns only the identifier and name, so on macOS it skips the per-id `--pkg-info` round trip entirely (the name is derived from the identifier alone).

The macOS legs buffer every row locally and commit only after the whole acquisition completes, because `write_output` only appends — a mid-walk pkgutil failure can never leave a partial mix of real rows and an error line. A degraded run (pkgutil timeout, kill, spawn failure, truncation, or nonzero exit) emits a single `error|...` row and returns rc=1 instead of a partial or empty list read as complete.

`list_inventory` is the third action, built for the daily installed-software inventory (`ecosystem` `msi`, `kind` `pkg`). On Windows it walks `MsiEnumProductsExW` in the machine install context only (`szUserSid` must be NULL for that context) and reads `InstalledProductName`, `VersionString` and `Publisher` per product with `MsiGetProductInfoExW`. It uses the wide Ex APIs throughout, because the ANSI variants return the system code page and corrupt non-ASCII names; `list` and `product_codes` stay on `MsiEnumProductsA`/`MsiGetProductInfoA` on purpose (their behaviour is frozen: every visible install context, `-` placeholders, a sentinel row). A product installed only for one user is never listed by `list_inventory`. macOS answers `unsupported` (`installed_apps.list_inventory` owns the pkgutil receipt roster) and Linux answers `unsupported` (no Windows Installer). The row builder is a pure header (`msi_packages_inventory.hpp`) with the Windows Installer calls injected, so it is unit-tested on every OS from a committed real capture. `execute()` wraps all three actions in one `try/catch`, so an exception can never cross the plugin ABI; it reports `status|<action>|constrained|msi_packages:exception`, `UNAVAILABLE`/`PARTIAL`, rc 1.

This plugin is deliberately narrow: it is the honest MSI/pkgutil view only, never coercing a macOS reverse-domain identifier into a fabricated Windows-shaped GUID, and it does not attempt the broader dpkg/rpm/pacman/Homebrew/registry inventory that `installed_apps` already covers.

outputs_note:
Pipe-delimited rows. `list` rows use the literal discriminator `msi`; `product_codes` rows use the literal discriminator `product_code`; `list_inventory` rows use `inv`, led by exactly one `status` row. Every dynamic macOS field is pipe/newline-escaped before being written, so an identifier, version, or path containing `|` or a newline can never shift columns or inject a row. `-` means the underlying property was empty or absent — it never means the plugin failed to read it (a failed acquisition is instead reported as a single `error|...` row and a nonzero return code, never as a placeholder data row).



`list_inventory` grammar (the daily sync reads it): row 0 is `status|list_inventory|<supported|constrained|unsupported>|<tokens or ->`, then one `inv|<product_code>|<name>|<version>|<publisher>` per machine-context product. Honest-empty: a property that cannot be read is an EMPTY field, never `-`, and there is no sentinel row (zero products is the status row and nothing else). The `|`, tab, CR and LF characters are deleted from the dynamic fields (the collector splits on raw `|` and never unescapes, so an escaped pipe would shift the columns); a backslash is kept. `product_code` is carried exactly as the product registers it, with no case normalisation (a real machine registers some codes in lower case). `InstallLocation` and `UninstallString` are not emitted (the inventory's reserved slots 13-14, #5186), and `InstallSource` is not read. Status tokens: `windows:msi_enum:<winerror>`, `macos:owned_by_installed_apps`, `linux:no_msi`, `msi_packages:exception`.

Two additional macOS-only sentinel rows exist outside the schema above: `msi|__truncated__|<total_seen>|-|-` when a `list` receipt walk exceeds the 500-receipt cap (the tail is dropped, and this row states how many receipts were actually seen), and `msi|No packages found|-|-|-` / `product_code|none|-` when a clean walk finds zero receipts.

privileges.grant: None — `MsiEnumProductsA`/`MsiGetProductInfoA` (and `MsiEnumProductsExW`/`MsiGetProductInfoExW` for `list_inventory`) read the per-machine product registration table; the source requests no elevation.
privileges.if_refused: No explicit permission-denied handling in the leg; an empty enumeration falls through to the honest "no packages" sentinel row (`msi|No MSI packages found|-|-|-` / `product_code|none|-`) rather than a typed error. `list_inventory` does report it: an enumeration that ends with anything other than `ERROR_NO_MORE_ITEMS` is `status|list_inventory|constrained|windows:msi_enum:<code>`, `CONSTRAINED`/`PARTIAL`, with the rows read so far still emitted.
privileges.measured: `list`, `product_codes`: 2026-09-07 on bare metal as `SYSTEM`. `list_inventory`: 2026-10-17 on bare metal (Windows 11, build 26200) as `SYSTEM` and as an admin user, with identical machine lists; a non-elevated identity is unmeasured

privileges.grant: None — `pkgutil` reads local receipt databases that do not require root. The captured sample below was taken unprivileged.
privileges.if_refused: A degraded pkgutil run (timeout, kill, spawn failure, truncation, or nonzero exit) emits one `error|msi_packages: acquisition degraded (...)` row and rc=1 rather than a partial or empty list read as complete.
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, root by default today (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md` TL;DR; narrowing tracked in #1455)

privileges.if_refused: `list` and `product_codes` unconditionally return `error|platform not supported` and rc=1; `list_inventory` answers `status|list_inventory|unsupported|linux:no_msi` and rc=0.

result_status.when: `list` and `product_codes`: they never set a typed status (the sample blocks show `UNDECLARED / UNKNOWN /`).

`list_inventory` on Windows: the enumeration ended with `ERROR_NO_MORE_ITEMS`. Zero products is a complete answer (the status row alone). A product whose property cannot be read is also `OK`: it is listed with that field empty and no token.

`list_inventory` on Windows: `MsiEnumProductsExW` returned a code other than success or `ERROR_NO_MORE_ITEMS` (for example `1610`). The walk stops there, the rows read so far follow the status row, and the daily sync skips its whole cycle.
`list_inventory` on macOS: unsupported by design; `installed_apps.list_inventory` owns the pkgutil receipt roster.
`list_inventory` on Linux: there is no Windows Installer.

Any action, any OS: something threw. `execute()` catches it, writes `status|<action>|constrained|msi_packages:exception` (the level is `constrained` while the typed status is `UNAVAILABLE`: the command failed, rc 1) with this fixed token, never the exception's own text, and never lets the exception cross the plugin ABI.

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result only.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore (default 90-day retention), queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`. `list` is additionally aggregatable by `name` with a `count` operation; `product_codes` carries no aggregation.

**`list_inventory` feeds the daily installed-software sync** (ADR-0016): the agent collects it as `ecosystem` `msi`, `kind` `pkg`, `package_id` = the product code, `source` `msi_packages.list_inventory`. `list` and `product_codes` are not consumed by it, the TAR warehouse, DEX or metrics — nothing else runs on a schedule, and the only other production references to `msi_packages` are the server's dashboard key-value column-rendering fallback and its MCP workflow-catalog blurb, both cosmetic.

**Sensitivity.** `list`/`product_codes` rows are an installed-software inventory: `product_code`, `name`, and `version` name specific installed packages (e.g. `Office 16 Click-to-Run Extensibility Component`); `install_location` is a filesystem path that could occasionally embed a username under a user profile, though no row in the sample captures does. No device id, MAC, or hostname is emitted.
**Siblings:** `installed_apps.list` / `.query` (the broader dpkg/rpm/pacman/apk/Homebrew/registry software inventory this plugin deliberately does not duplicate).

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("windows.software.msi.list")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`.
